# 12. Routine reference

Every code entry of the main program, in address order by module (`src/stage1/<module>.asm`). The name, the title and
the description are the source's (`src/stage1/stage1.ann`); the rest is what the recordings saw: `work/stage1/c1o` (c1's stage 1 play window (frames 15476-16658)), `work/stage2/rec/rzx-r1` (rzx-r1: the RZX run's stage 1 replayed pass by pass), and the case's other recordings (`case.json` `read_builds`, `code_builds`): their calls in a Runs row of their own, their callers, callees, reads and writes (`read_builds` only) with the others'. They are local, not in the repository; the WALKTHROUGH's commands rebuild them.
Runs count the calls of the entry itself; the time is its own t-states (callees excluded) and their share
of the recording. Memory ranges name the label at or below their first byte (inner labels too, `Label+offset`)
and the entries they cover. The interrupt's acceptance (the vector read, the return address pushed) is
the handler's, not the interrupted routine's. An entry no recording reached says so; one the case's other
recordings ran gives their calls.
Written by `kit/refdocs.py`; edit `src/stage1/stage1.ann`, then run `kit/mkgame.py --case . --install`
(see [3. Build and load](03-build-and-load.md)) and `kit/refdocs.py --case .`.
The parts of the medium (`case.json` `ref_parts`: The resident (TZX blocks 25, 17, 27 at `$F000-$FFFF`), The front
(TZX block 37), Stage 2 (TZX block 43), Stage 3 (TZX block 46), Stage 4 (TZX block 49), Stage 5 (TZX block 52), The
tape BASIC (TZX block 2), The decryption chain and the SpeedLock loader, The second stage (TZX block 7), Unxor (TZX
block 29), Sl1End (TZX block 31), Boot (TZX blocks 33 and 35)) follow the main program, each under its own heading
with its modules, its source, its annotations and its recordings.

### `StageEntry` (`$7800`)

**Start the stage: lives from H, variables, HUD, the first room, then the main loop**

Called by the resident stage loader with H = the lives left. Stores H in Lives, then: `$9DA1` (clears `$FE08-$FE5F`, the carried items from StartItems, the item window at slot 6, the energy refill `$2E`), `$97AC` (the title, the HUD), `$921E` and `$922F`, RoomGrid = `$9B6F` (grid 0) with the actor list pointer `$FE25` = `$9BA0`, `$A4A1` and `$A47D` (the room's actors), RoomNumber = 2, `$A444` (clears the room cells), ClearBuffer, `$A5BD`, `$A5DF` (draws the actors) and CopyBuffer, then runs on into MainLoop.

Witness: L1 3 (rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

## mainloop

`src/stage1/mainloop.asm`

### `MainLoop` (`$7839`)

**One pass: pace, HUD, input, actors, draw, copy; SPACE opens the item window**

The pass, in order: PacePass, ShowPieceTaken, FlashPieces, CheckPause (ENTER), `$8D1D`, RedrawItemsIfChanged, ClearBuffer, CheckStageExit (may leave to EndStage), the missiles `$B2E6`, `$A5BD`, `$A5DF` (the actors drawn into the buffer), `$89BB`, `$8A2E`, `$8930`, `$A28B`, KeyHook, `$8CAA` (attributes and CopyBuffer), `$984D` (energy, lives flash, game over step), ShowScore, then the SPACE test `$8A54`.

SPACE with CAPS SHIFT ends the stage with E = 1 (QuitStage); SPACE alone opens ItemWindow unless the hero is in state `$0F` (dying; the hero record's +`$0A` at `$74EA`). The loop goes on while Lives is not 0 or the hero's state is not 0; with no lives and the hero back in state 0 it ends with E = 0 (GameOverExit).

Witness: L1 19500 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

### `EndStage` (`$789E`)

**Leave the stage: hide the HUD boxes, save the HUD, fade, return E, H = lives, BC = the score's digits**

E (pushed) is the outcome: 0 game over (GameOverExit), 1 quit (QuitStage), 2 stage completed (StageExit). Clears the play buffer, hides the pieces boxes and the lives boxes with two inline attribute fills (`$8C3D`), saves the HUD attributes (rows 0-5) to `$7600`, clears the score, the two middle HUD fields, the item strip and the pieces field with CopyToScreen from the cleared buffer (stride 0), saves the HUD bitmap (lines 0-47) to `$7000` (`$8A89`), fades the screen (FlashFadeScreen), clears it (`$8B92`), waits 100 frames (`$8C35`) and returns to the stage loader with E, BC = ScoreDigitsHigh (the six score digits) and H = Lives.

Witness: L1 2 (rzx-r1, s1-right).

### `PacePass` (`$795D`)

**Reseed the random pointer every 64 passes and pad the pass with a busy wait in the light rooms**

When PassCounter & `$3F` is 0, the high byte of RandomPointer is set from R. Then: in grid 0 (GridNumber 0), rooms 0-5 wait `$044C` rounds of DelayBC; in grid 1, room 0 waits `$0640` (PaceShaftRoom); every other room goes on at once. The wait evens out the pass time of rooms with few actors (8978 of the 10187 passes in the stage-1 recordings waited).

Witness: L1 19500 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

### `CheckPause` (`$79B1`)

**ENTER pauses: wait for its release, a second press and its release**

Reads port `$BFFE` bit 0 (ENTER). Not pressed: returns at once. Pressed: waits for the key's release, the next press and its release, so the game stands still between two presses. No other effect.

### `FlashFadeScreen` (`$7925`)

**Fade every coloured ink up to white over 7 frames, then down to black over 7 frames**

Seven times (HALT each): every attribute whose ink is neither 0 nor 7 gets ink + 1. Then seven times (two HALTs each): every ink not 0 gets ink - 1. Inputs: none; changes the whole attribute area `$5800-$5AFF`. Called by EndStage.

### `CopyToScreen` (`$79CC`)

**Copy a block of bytes to the screen, line by line**

Inputs: HL = the source, B = the screen column, C = the first pixel line, D = the width in bytes, E = the lines, A = the source's stride (added to HL after each line; 0 repeats one source line, used with the cleared buffer to clear a screen block). Patches the column into `$79E5` and the stride into `$79F6`, then for each line takes the line's address from ScreenLineTable and LDIRs D bytes. Destroys IX, BC, DE.

Witness: L1 20920 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

### `PreShiftSprite` (`$7F4D`)

**For an actor with a shift (+`$11` = 1-7): copy its sprite to `$7640` and shift it right**

IY = the actor record. +`$11` = 0 or `$64` and up: nothing. Else copies the sprite (+4/+5, +2 bytes wide, +3 lines) to `$7640` with a zero byte added to each line, then shifts each line right by +`$11` pixels with the routine ShiftRoutines[+`$11`] (patched into PreShiftCall). Called by `$A62A` for every actor drawn.

Witness: L1 108073 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right). The shift was 0 in every pass of c1o, deaths, s1-idle and s1-right; rzx-r1 takes the copy from `$7F53` on 595 times (the warrior's flying head, moved in eighths by StepFineBack).

### `PlotRow1` (`$8776`)

**Plot one sprite row 1 byte wide into the play buffer**

HL = the sprite's bytes, DE = the buffer address. ORs (HL) into (DE) (no mask: the buffer is cleared every pass),

then HL + 1 and DE + 32 (the next pixel line). One of the row plotters of RowPlotters `$8910`, called once a row by

the sprite drawer at `$A6AA`. The plotters 1-7 bytes wide all work so; the mirrored ones read the row's bytes in

order and write them right to left through the bit-reversal table at `$FA00` (resident), so a sprite faces left.

Witness: L1 289583 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

**Copy the open cells' attributes from the shadow, then CopyBuffer**

The play area's 18 rows x 28 columns from row 6 column 2: where the cell kind (`$7282`, BuildSpans) is 0 (open),

the attribute comes from the shadow `$6DC2` (the room's colours with the actors' painted in); solid cells keep

theirs. Then CopyBuffer. With RestoreAttributes = 1 (set at `$9FB2`): clears it, CopyBuffer first, then after a

HALT every cell is written: open cells from the shadow, solid cells from RoomAttributes `$7042`.

### `BuildSpans` (`$99E9`)

**Turn the cells into tile kinds and list the open runs as spans for CopyBuffer**

Patches `$9A1C` with the tile kinds' address (`$5B0A` + the header word `$5B00`). Each cell's tile number becomes its

kind (0 open, else solid scenery). Each run of open cells in a row becomes a span (AddSpan): 6 bytes from `$76A0`:

the length in cells, 0, the play buffer's address, the screen's address. SpanCount = the spans.

### `CopyBuffer` (`$9ADA`)

**Copy the open spans of the play buffer to the screen (an LDI chain cut by a patched JP)**

SP walks the span table `$76A0` (POP BC: the length, POP HL: the buffer, POP DE: the screen). For each span: patches

the LD BC at `$9B45` with 32 - the length, writes JP `$9B45` into the LDI chain at `$9B09` + 2 x the length (saved at

`$9B50`), the LD E at `$9B49` with the screen address's low byte; copies 8 lines (LDIs, then HL + 32 - length, E

back, D + 1); puts ED A0 ED back. SpanCount spans; interrupts off meanwhile.

Witness: L1 19503 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

### `DrawActorSprite` (`$A6AA`)

**Draw B lines of the actor's frame into the play buffer, then colour it**

Input: B lines, DE = the buffer, HL = the frame (rows of +2 bytes, top first, no mask). +9 bit 0: copied opaque (DrawActorOpaque). Else ORed in by a row routine from the table `$8910` (4 bytes a width 0-7: the right-facing and the left-facing routine); the left-facing routines mirror the bytes through the resident bit-reverse table `$FA00` and step left, so a left-facing actor's X is its right column. A shifted copy (+`$11` 1-99) is one byte wider. The routine is written into RowDrawCall. Then ColourActor.

Witness: L1 108073 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

**Move one star down by its speed and plot it as two pixel lines**

IX = the star: +0 speed 1-4, +1 the pixel within the byte 0-3, +2 the column 2-29, +3 y (`$80` and up: not yet on screen). Off screen: y += speed only. On screen: y = (y + speed) mod 128, clears the bytes above it (speed lines, from ScreenLineTable+96, line 48 down), and plots two lines from StarPixels (speed and pixel).

### `DissolveHud` (`$8AB1`)

**Dissolve the HUD's 48 pixel lines onto the screen in 8 steps**

DE = the source picture (48 lines of 32 bytes; `$7000` from StageSetUp `$97AC`: the HUD as loaded). Eight steps, each

after a HALT: every byte of screen lines 0-47 = source AND a mask; the mask is DissolveMasks `$F9CB` + set + step

(set = bits 3-4 of a ROM byte read through RandomPointer, 0, 8, 16 or 24; the step 0-7, the ADD at DissolveStepOperand set to 0 first) and gains bits each step until `$FF`; only RandomPointer's low byte is cleared each step, so each step reads the next 6 pages of the ROM and the pattern changes (rzx-r1: the first reads of the 8 steps at `$0701`, `$0D01`, `$1301` ... `$3101`). Patches the

LD DE at `$8AC5` (the source) and the ADD A at `$8AE9` (the step).

Witness: L1 3 (rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

### `ItemWindow` (`$7C27`)

**SPACE: stop the game, flash the strip's frame, choose an item with LEFT and RIGHT, SPACE again to go on**

Clears PassCounter, waits (cycling the frame colours, CycleWindowFrame) for SPACE's release, then every 6 frames: DrawItemStrip and ShowItemCount; RIGHT scrolls to the previous slot (ScrollItemsRight), LEFT to the next (ScrollItemsLeft); SPACE again: waits for its release, cycles the frame back to its first colour and flashes the selected box (FlashSelectedBox).

### `HeroUpdate` (`$AC3D`)

**The hero's pass: items, hazards, weapons, colour, then his state's handler**

IY = the hero. Item 1 drains (`$89A1`). A deadly cell (bit 3) on his head row (his top line, IY+1), one column ahead of him (CellAt

`$B162` with E = his column + 4 facing right or his column facing left: screen column X + 2 or X - 2), or his column 0 or 32 and up, costs a life (LoseLife `$7ECE`) unless he is dying (state

`$0F`). Then, not dying: the selected item's kind (`$7F05`) fires its weapon: 7 FireBolt `$AD14`, 5 ThrowAmmo `$AD4B`, 8

`$92D1`. Dying: the death pause (`$9259`). Then the colour (HeroColour `$ACD9`), and while HeroFreeze `$FE58` counts down

the controls are ignored. Else by the state +`$0A`: 0 HeroStand `$ADA2`, 1 HeroWalk `$AF64`, 2 HeroJump `$B087`, 3

### `HeroDeath` (`$B22B`)

**Start the hero's death: a burst of eight fragments, the hero hidden, the pause**

Only when no death is in progress (RespawnShiftX `$FE56` = `$FF`). E = the pause in pairs of passes (`$33` after a life, `$6C`

after the last; from LoseLife `$7ECE`), stored in the hero's +`$10` (`$74F0`). Clears the effects 8-15 (`$7610-$763F`),

adds eight effects of type 7 at the hero (column, line + 4) with +4 = 0, 2, .. 14 (the directions) and +5 = the

column x 2 (AddMissileHigh `$B296`), sets state `$0F` (`$74EA`), takes the respawn point (`$927C`: D column, E line),

RespawnShiftX and RespawnShiftY `$FE57` from it, and hides the hero (column 0, line `$8C`, colour 0).

Witness: L1 7 (c1o, deaths, s1-right).

### `UpdatePathFlyer` (`$842C`)

**Kinds 7 and 8: a flyer along PathSteps, forwards (7) then back (8); OR-drawn 3 x 13 bytes**

+4 = the step into PathSteps (pairs: dx in half columns, dy), +5 = x in half columns, +3 a step counter. Kind 7 steps forwards; at the end mark (`$64`) it becomes kind 8 and is moved by RespawnShiftX (x 2) and RespawnShiftY, unless no lives are left (freed). ### `StrikeableActor` (`$A7C4`)

**Per-pass handler of an actor that the hero's low strike hits (two hits destroy it)**

Its address is the handler word at `$9CA6`, `$9CAF`, `$9CB8` and `$9CC1` of the room data (UpdateActors `$A5BD` calls the

record's +6/+7). IY = the actor record. When the hero's low strike lands this pass (`$7FEE`: hero state 7 at frame

4) and InStrikeReach `$A816` says the actor is in front of the hero, the hit count (the record's +8, which is also

the frame number) goes up: an odd count plays effect 2 and the actor shows its damaged frame; an even one destroys

it: score +20 and an explosion (`$A065`), the actor marked dead in the grid's actor list (`$A48E`), then by the

record's +`$10` bits 0-1: 2 drops the object at `$A0D6`, 1 the object at `$A0C3`, 0 bursts it into eight fragments

(ShatterActor `$A803`).

Each pass it shows frame (+8) of the frame table `$E25A` over the graphics at `$E190` (SetActorFrame `$AA02`). In

stage 1 these are the urns and chests (kinds 3-6 of ActorKinds); the hit path runs in rzx-r1 (frames 638 and

662: placement 2 of room 2 struck twice).

Witness: L1 24767 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

### `FragmentActor` (`$A891`)

**Per-pass handler of a fragment: fly an arc, land, lie, sink, be picked up**

The handler word of the fragment template (`$9D71`). IY = the fragment. Its colour alternates (ColourRedMagenta

`$B377`). The step counter +`$0B` runs from 0: steps 5, `$0E`, `$14` and `$17` play effect 3 (a bounce); each step moves

it by +8 pixels a pass across (MoveFragment `$A97A`, reversed when facing left) and down by the step's entry of

FragmentArc0 `$A9CA` (arc +`$0A` = 0) or FragmentArc1 `$A9E6` (other arcs; doubled when +`$0A` bit 1 is set); from step

`$18` it no longer moves across. At steps 9, `$10`, `$15` and `$17` it looks at the cell under it (column + 2, line +

`$16`, `$14` or `$0E`; CellAt `$B162`): no solid ground there makes it fall (step `$1C`: 7 lines a pass, removed under line

`$90`). Step `$1B` is the rest (FragmentRest `$A91D`): +`$0E` counts down; under 6 it sinks 3 lines a pass and at 0 it is

removed. A fragment the hero touches (his column or the one left of it, his line within `$20`) is taken: the pending

energy change EnergyChange `$FE4E` + 6, score +25, effect 5, and it is removed.

Witness: L1 2817 (rzx-r1).

### `MoveFragment` (`$A97A`)

**Move the fragment E pixels across and point it at its pre-shifted image**

IY = the fragment, E = the pixels (negated when it faces left, +9 bit 7). The pixel column (+0 x 8 + the

sub-column +`$0D`) moves by E; +0 and +`$0D` take the new column and pixel. The image pointer +4/+5 = `$E9E4` + `$21` x

the shift (Multiply `$8B24`; the shift is the pixel, or 7 - the pixel when it faces left): eight pre-shifted copies

of 33 bytes. A fragment that reaches column 0 or 31 is removed (RemoveActor `$B35E`).

### `StartBurst` (`$A1F3`)

**Turn a 16 x 12 shape into particles at `$7040` that fly apart (UpdateBurst)**

Input: A = BurstSmall (1 small: 14 steps; 0 big: 28), D, E = the shape's left column and top cell row, IX = the shape (12 rows of 2 bytes, bit 7 left), B and C = the two inks. PlaySoundVector 1, RandomPointer = `$0D7A` (every burst flies the same way), the colours C, C + `$40` (bright), B, B + `$40` into ParticleInks, BurstTimer = `$FF`. Each set bit of the shape gives a particle record of 4 bytes at `$7040`: X, Y (cell row), the direction (a random 0-5, + 13 for the right byte), the ink (a random 0-3); `$FF` ends the list. Preserves IY. rzx-r1: frame 661, T 10312 (effect 1 through StartBurstSound).

### `UpdateBurst` (`$A28B`)

**Move and draw the burst's particles one step (every pass)**

Called by the main loop. Nothing while BurstTimer = `$64`. Else BurstTimer + 1; at the last step (`$1C`, or `$0E` when BurstSmall) it ends (StopBurst). The step picks the particles' glyph: `$EE86`[step + a random 0-3] x 8 + `$EE66`, written into ParticleGlyph. Each particle (4 bytes from `$7040`, `$FF` ends, `$80` dead): its direction's step table at `$EEA9` + direction x 32 gives an index into BurstSteps (dx, dy; the second set for directions 13 and up), X + dx kept within 1-30, Y - dy (a particle above row 0 or below row 17 dies: `$80`); then the 8 glyph bytes are stored into the play buffer at the cell and the cell's attribute (ParticleInks) via `$B34E`.

### `LoadRoomActors` (`$A4CC`)

**Free the actors not kept over a room change and create the room's placed actors**

Frees every record of `$74F2-$75DB` without +`$0F` bit 1. Then walks Placements (3 bytes: the kind, bit 7 done; X and Y in cells over the whole grid; `$FF` ends). A placement not done inside the room window (X in 2 x RoomColumn to + 29, Y in 2 x RoomRow to + 17) takes a free record found from `$75CA` down (no lower bound: it is assumed there is one) and is filled from the kind table `$9C8A` (9 bytes a kind: Y offset in lines, the handler, five bytes for +8..+`$0C`, +`$0F`): X and Y relative to the room (Y in lines + the offset), the entry X, Y, +`$10` = the placement's index, width 1, height 8, +`$11` = 0, and a random 0-63 for +`$0A` when the kind gives `$40`.

Called by the room builder at each room change.

### `SetActorFrame` (`$AA02`)

**Set the actor IY to frame A of a frame table (the 4 bytes after the CALL)**

The CALL is followed by two words: the frame table DE and the graphics base BC; the routine pops them and

returns to its caller's caller. A frame record is 6 bytes (FrameRecordAddress `$B12A`: DE + 6A): +0 the column

offset (negated when the actor faces left, +9 bit 7), +1 the line offset, +2 the width in bytes, +3 the height in

lines, +4/+5 the offset of the image from the graphics base. The actor's column +0 = the offset + its base column

+`$0D`, its line +1 = the line offset + its base line +`$0E`, +2 and +3 the size, +4/+5 the image address. An image is

width x height bytes, row by row, one bit a pixel, no mask (DrawSprite `$B42B` copies it).

Witness: L1 58036 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

### `AddMissile` (`$B28D`)

**Add a missile (shot, spark) to the first eight slots of the missile records `$75E0`**

In: D column, E line, C type, B and A its parameters. The list holds 16 records of 6 bytes: +0 column (`$FF` free),

+1 line, +2 type (the handler of MissileHandlers `$B31A`), +3 `$FF`, +4 B, +5 A. The search starts after the slot of

MissileCursor `$FE27` (round robin over 8). A = `$FA` puts a Random `$8B85` byte in +5. Out: Z when the eight slots are

full (nothing added), else NZ. AddMissileHigh `$B296` uses slots 8-15 (`$7610`).

### `RoomChange` (`$988B`)

**Build the room: unpack the stage's graphics, draw the scenery, make the spans**

BurstTimer = 100. Unrle `$A424` the packed tiles and map `$B4B2` into `$5B00` (the play buffer), clear the shots, build

the cells (RoomCells, IX = RoomGrid), `$A057`, then patch the tile bitmaps' and the attributes' addresses into `$98F1`

and `$98D3` (from the header words `$5B02`, `$5B04`) and draw every cell of the 18 x 28 play area: its attribute into

the shadow `$6DC2` and its 8 bitmap bytes straight onto the screen (CopyTileToScreen, from line 48 column 2). Then

BuildSpans, ClearBuffer (the unpacked data is gone) and the actors (JP `$A4CC`).

Witness: L1 101 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

### `Unrle` (`$A424`)

**Unpack an RLE block: the first byte is the escape, ESC n v is n copies of v, ESC ESC ends**

Input: HL = the packed block, DE = the output. The block's first byte is its escape byte, written into UnrleEscape and UnrleEnd's compares. Then: a byte other than the escape is copied; the escape followed by n, v writes n copies of v (n = 0 gives 256); the escape twice ends. Output: HL = the second escape of the end mark, DE = after the output.

The room builder `$988B` unpacks the stage's tiles and map at `$B4B2` with it to `$5B00` at every room change (26 calls in the stage-1 recordings).

Witness: L1 101 (c1o, deaths, rzx-r1, s1-idle, s1-right).

### The resident (TZX blocks 25, 17, 27 at `$F000-$FFFF`): init

`src/resident/init.asm`

#### `PlayStage` (`$F1CA`)

**Show the titles, load the stage at IY (unless loaded), run it; Z when it was completed**

Input: IY a StageTable record. ClearScreen; if StageLoaded is not the record's stage, PRESS PLAY ON TAPE, WaitFrames, and the line cleared again. The two titles with PrintRecord. Then StageLoadLoop: LoadStage until it gives Z (the right block, StageCheck), each failure marking no stage loaded. SilenceAy, ClearScreen, H := Lives, CALL GameMain (the stage), Lives := H, CP E with 2, SilenceAy. Output: Z when the stage ended with E = 2 (completed), BC the address of the stage's score digits for GameOver. Witness: L1 8 (c1, joystick, menu, rzx-r0-rzx-r4).

#### `GameOver` (`$F24B`)

**GAME OVER: a credit less, the menu RESTART THIS STAGE / RESTART FROM STAGE ONE, SPACE chooses**

Input: BC the address of the stage's six score digits (copied into the menu's SCORE). Credits := Credits - 1 (the POKE "credits 62045,0" is the DEC A at `$F25D`, src/tape notes), shown as a digit. ClearScreen, GAME OVER, PRESS SPACE TO SELECT, 20 rounds of HALT + CycleColours (which HALTs again): 40 frames, the menu. Every 64 frames (32 rounds of two HALTs, FrameCounter AND `$1F` = 0) the highlight moves to the other line (with no credit left it stays on RESTART FROM STAGE ONE); SPACE takes the highlighted one: RESTART THIS STAGE sets Lives := 5 and returns (PlayStage again), RESTART FROM STAGE ONE drops the return and jumps to RestartFromStageOne. Witness: L1 4 (s1-right, s2-right, s3-right, s4-right).

#### `TextToBuffer` (`$F3CB`)

**Draw the text at IY (column byte, bit, row, text, 0) into TextBuffer with PrintFont**

Clears TextBuffer, sets BitShift and TextRow; for each character: A-Z, a space (as the glyph after Z) and 0-9 (after the space); the glyph's width mask to CharMask, its 7 rows to GlyphBuffer, shifted right by BitShift, ORed into TextBuffer at DE; then Advance. Ends after the 0 with IY past it. Witness: L1 54 (c1, joystick, menu, s1-right, s2-right, s3-right, s4-right, stageload, rzx-r0-rzx-r4).

#### `RevealText` (`$F483`)

**Bring TextBuffer onto the screen from pixel row A in 8 frames through the dissolve masks**

For step 0-7: the ADD A,n at RevealMaskAdd := `$CB` + step; HALT, CycleColours; for the 7 rows and 32 bytes: mask = DissolveMasks set (a ROM byte from `$0001` up AND `$18`) at the step; screen := (screen AND NOT mask) OR (buffer AND mask). Witness: L1 54 (c1, joystick, menu, s1-right, s2-right, s3-right, s4-right, stageload, rzx-r0-rzx-r4).

### The resident (TZX blocks 25, 17, 27 at `$F000-$FFFF`): stageload

`src/resident/stageload.asm`

#### `LoadStage` (`$F5E4`)

**Load stage C's block (B, H, L its length) unless it is the one loaded; Z when it is in memory**

Inputs: C the stage (0 the front), B, H, L the length parameters (to LoadLength). StageLoaded = C: wait 120 frames, Z. Else StageLoaded := C, HALT, LoadBlock; NZ (a wrong block or a load error) returns NZ; else clear the line, STOP THE TAPE, WaitFrames, Z. Witness: L1 7 (c1, joystick, menu, stageload, rzx-r0, rzx-r1).

#### `LoadBlock` (`$FF54`)

**Load the next block with TurboLoad; with a stage wanted, check its byte at StageCheckByte; Z when right**

DI; Im2Jump := SavedLoaderBytes (the loader's code); TurboLoad; SaveLoaderBytes; SetIm2 (Im2Handler). StageLoaded 0 (the front): Z. Else Z when the byte at StageCheckByte equals StageCheck's for StageLoaded, NZ for another stage's block. A load error does not return here: TurboExit's RST 8 ends in the ROM's error report. Witness: L1 7 (c1, joystick, menu, stageload, rzx-r0, rzx-r1).

## The front (TZX block 37) (`src/front/front.json`)

Myth: History in the Making, System 3 Software 1989: the main block (TZX block 37), 15 360 bytes at `$6C3F`: the
logo, the credits, the menu. Its entries are `src/front/<module>.asm`, written from `src/front/front.ann` by
`kit/mkgame.py --part src/front/front.json`; the recordings: `work/stage1/c1` (c1: a 48K from power-on, the whole
load at signal speed, the menu, stage 1), and `work/stage1/rec/menu`.

#### `DissolveLogoBox` (`$7889`)

**Wipe pixel lines 64-127, columns 7-24 to paper in 8 dissolve steps, the masks picked by ROM bytes**

For step 0-7: the ADD A,n at `$78C4` gets `$CB` + step; for each of the 64 lines from ScreenLineTable+128 (`$FB80`, line 64; DissolveLinePtr `$9718` walks it) and each of its 18 bytes from column 7: BC = PixelShift's word + 1 (stored back), A = (BC) AND `$18`, mask = the byte at `$F900` + A + `$CB` + step (the resident's dissolve masks `$F9CB-$F9EA`: four sets of 8, each set ending in `$FF`), screen byte := screen AND NOT mask. The word starts at 0, so the bytes that pick the mask set are the ROM's from `$0001` up: a fixed pseudo-random pattern. After step 7 every mask is `$FF` and the 64 x 18 bytes are 0. No HALT: the 8 steps run back to back.

c1 (the front's bytes): `$7891` 8 runs, `$78A7` 512, `$78B7` 9216 (8 x 64 x 18), right after SPACE at frame 7938.

Witness: L1 2 (c1, rzx-r0).

#### `ShimmerFrame` (`$79AE`)

**Count ShimmerCount down and copy the shimmer pattern at its phase over the box's 10 x 20 attributes**

ShimmerCount `$FE1D` - 1; phase = (ShimmerCount >> 1) AND 31; for row 0-9: 20 bytes from ShimmerColours `$78E2` + phase + row to the attributes at `$58E6` + 32 x row (row 7, column 6 down). The phase moves every second call and the pattern repeats every 32 bytes, so at the usual two frames a call the streaks slide one cell every 4 frames and come round every 128 frames.

Then IY + 15, IX + 7. After the five: ClearTextLine with the lines 68, 84, 100, 116 and back to Menu (BackToMenu `$9807`).

#### `PrintText` (`$9D72`)

**Print the text after the CALL into TextBuffer and reveal it on its screen line; return after its zero byte**

In: (SP) = the parameters: font, start byte, pixel shift, screen line, text, 0. FontBase `$A0D7` := FontSmall `$9ED2` for font 0, else FontLarge `$9FFA`; TextBuffer `$5B00-$5BFF` := 0; D, E = `$5B`, the start byte; PixelShift `$A0D2` := the shift; TextLine `$A0D3` := the line. Each character: 0 ends; "A"-"Z" give glyph 0-25; a space glyph 26; any other byte under "A": byte - `$30` + `$5C` - `$41` (the digits 0-9: glyphs 27-36). The glyph's 8 bytes at FontBase + 8 x glyph: GlyphMask `$A0D4` := its width mask, its 7 rows into GlyphRows `$7600` (each followed by a zero byte), shifted right PixelShift times through the pair, ORed into the buffer at DE, DE + 32 a row. AdvanceColumn `$9E24` moves the pen by the glyph's width + 1 pixels. At the end: RevealStrip `$9E4D` with A = TextLine, then RET past the zero byte (IY pushed).

c1 (the front's bytes): 14 calls, frames 8007-8539; menu: 27 (DEFINE KEYS's prompts and names, the menu's lines, the wipes).

#### `RevealStrip` (`$9E4D`)

**Copy TextBuffer's 7 lines (columns 7-24) to the screen at line A in 8 dissolve steps of two frames**

In: A = the screen line. RevealLines `$A0D5` := ScreenLineTable + 2A. For step 0-7: the ADD A,n at `$9E98` := `$CB` + step; HALT, ShimmerFrame, PaintBoxColours, HALT; then for the 7 lines and their 18 bytes from column 7: the next ROM byte (PixelShift's word as a pointer, from 0 + 1 up) AND `$18` picks one of the four mask sets of the resident's dissolve masks `$F9CB`, mask = that set's byte for the step; screen := (screen AND NOT mask) OR (buffer AND mask). The masks grow to `$FF` by step 7, so after 16 frames the strip is the buffer's.

c1 (the front's bytes): 14 runs (one a printed line); menu: 27.

Witness: L1 146 (c1, joystick, menu, rzx-r0).

### Stage 2 (TZX block 43): entry

`src/stage2/entry.asm`

#### `StageEntry` (`$7800`)

**Start the stage: lives from H, variables, HUD, the first room, then the main loop**

Called by the resident stage loader (`$F239`) with H = the lives left. ### Stage 2 (TZX block 43): mainloop

`src/stage2/mainloop.asm`

#### `MainLoop` (`$7837`)

**One pass: HUD, input, actors, draw, copy; SPACE opens the item window**

The pass, in order: PacePassEmpty, ShowPieceTaken, FlashPieces, CheckPause (ENTER), SpawnTimer `$8D45`, RedrawItemsIfChanged, ClearBuffer, CheckStageExit (may leave to EndStage), UpdateMissiles, `$9EAE`, RunActorHandlers, `$9E4F`, DrawActors, `$9E21`, `$9C92`, HydraDefeated `$9BB4`, KeyHook, UpdateAttributes `$8CD0` (attributes and CopyBuffer), PassTick (energy, lives flash, game over step), ShowScore, then the SPACE test TestSpaceKey.

SPACE with CAPS SHIFT ends the stage with E = 1 (QuitStage); SPACE alone opens ItemWindow unless the hero is in state `$0F` (dying; the hero record's +`$0A` at `$74EA`). The loop goes on while Lives is not 0 or the hero's state is not 0; with no lives and the hero back in state 0 it ends with E = 0 (GameOverExit). rzx-r2 opened the item window 18 times; s2-right ends in game over at frame 5823.

Witness: L1 8032 (rzx-r2, s2-right, stageload).

#### `CopyToScreen` (`$7982`)

**Copy a block of bytes to the screen, line by line**

Inputs: HL = the source, B = the screen column, C = the first pixel line, D = the width in bytes, E = the lines, A = the source's stride (added to HL after each line; 0 repeats one source line, used with the cleared buffer to clear a screen block). Patches the column into `$799B` and the stride into `$79AC`, then for each line takes the line's address from ScreenLineTable and LDIRs D bytes. Destroys IX, BC, DE.

As in stage 1 at `$79CC`, the same code.

#### `PlotRow1` (`$88BF`)

**Plot one sprite row 1 byte wide into the play buffer**

HL = the sprite's bytes, DE = the buffer address. ORs (HL) into (DE) (no mask: the buffer is cleared every pass),

then HL + 1 and DE + 32 (the next pixel line). One of the row plotters of RowPlotters `$8A59`, called once a row by

the sprite drawer at DrawActorSprite `$A60E`. The plotters 1-7 bytes wide all work so; the mirrored ones read the row's bytes in

order and write them right to left through the bit-reversal table at `$FA00` (resident), so a sprite faces left.

#### `UpdateAttributes` (`$8CD0`)

**Copy the open cells' attributes from the shadow, then CopyBuffer**

The play area's 18 rows x 28 columns from row 6 column 2: where the cell kind (`$7282`, BuildSpans) is 0 (open), the attribute comes from the shadow `$6DC2` (the room's colours with the actors' painted in); solid cells keep theirs. #### `CopyBuffer` (`$94A9`)

**Copy the open spans of the play buffer to the screen (an LDI chain cut by a patched JP)**

SP walks the span table `$76A0` (POP BC: the length, POP HL: the buffer, POP DE: the screen). For each span: patches the LD BC at CopyLineEnd with 32 - the length, writes JP CopyLineEnd (`$C3` `$14` `$95` at `$94C8-$94CE`) into the LDI chain at CopyChain + 2 x the length (the place saved at CopySpanRestore), the LD E at CopyLineE with the screen address's low byte; copies 8 lines (LDIs, then HL + 32 - length, E back, D + 1); puts ED A0 ED back. SpanCount spans; interrupts off meanwhile. Called by UpdateAttributes every pass and by StageEntry.

As in stage 1 at `$9ADA`, the same code; the operands at `$94BC-$94D3` are its own labels and the bytes `$14` `$95` the low and high bytes of CopyLineEnd.

Witness: L1 8033 (rzx-r2, s2-right, stageload).

**Move one star down by its speed and plot it as two pixel lines**

IX = the star: +0 speed 1-4, +1 the pixel within the byte 0-3, +2 the column 2-29, +3 y (`$80` and up: not yet on screen). Off screen: y += speed only. #### `DissolveHud` (`$8AD6`)

**Dissolve the HUD's 48 pixel lines onto the screen in 8 steps**

DE = the source picture (48 lines of 32 bytes; `$7000` from StageSetUp `$9194`: the HUD as loaded). Eight steps, each after a HALT: every byte of screen lines 0-47 = source AND a mask; the mask is DissolveMasks `$F9CB` + set + step (set = bits 3-4 of a ROM byte read through RandomPointer, 0, 8, 16 or 24; the step 0-7, the ADD at DissolveStepOperand set to 0 first) and gains bits each step until `$FF`; only RandomPointer's low byte is cleared each step, so each step reads the next 6 pages of the ROM and the pattern changes (rzx-r1: the first reads of the 8 steps at `$0701`, `$0D01`, `$1301` ... `$3101`). Patches the LD DE at DissolveSource (the source) and the ADD A at DissolveStepOperand (the step). Both recordings: frames 80-112.

As in stage 1 at `$8AB1`.

Witness: L1 3 (rzx-r2, s2-right, stageload).

#### `ItemWindow` (`$7BF2`)

**SPACE: stop the game, flash the strip's frame, choose an item with LEFT and RIGHT, SPACE again to go on**

Clears PassCounter, waits (cycling the frame colours, CycleWindowFrame) for SPACE's release, then every 6 frames: DrawItemStrip and ShowItemCount; RIGHT scrolls to the previous slot (ScrollItemsRight), LEFT to the next (ScrollItemsLeft); SPACE again: waits for its release, cycles the frame back to its first colour (until the attribute at `$586A` is 1) and runs on into FlashSelectedBox. Called by MainLoop (`$7886`) when SPACE is pressed and the hero is not dying.

As in stage 1 at `$7C27`. In rzx-r2 the window opens 18 times (frames 520-18716): 14 scrolls right, 19 left; the last choice selects item 5 (the artefact) before the stage's exit.

**State 1: walk, 12 frames a cycle, 2 columns each half**

RIGHT while facing left, or LEFT while facing right, turns him (HeroTurn `$B234`). The frame goes 0 to `$0B`; at 0 and 6 the base column moves 2 (MoveBaseX `$B256`); then the frame of HeroWalkSet.

#### `HeroDeath` (`$B340`)

**Start the hero's death: a burst of eight fragments, the hero hidden, the pause**

Only when no death is in progress (RespawnShiftX `$FE64` = `$FF`). E = the pause in pairs of passes (`$33` from HeroFall `$B159`; LoseLife's `$7EBD`, `$7EC7`), stored in the hero's +`$10` (`$74F0`). Clears the missile slots 8-15 (`$7610-$763F`), adds eight missiles of type 7 at the hero (column, line + 4) with +4 = 0, 2, .. 14 (the directions) and +5 = the column x 2 (AddMissileHigh `$B3C5`), sets state `$0F` (`$74EA`), takes the respawn point (`$8F45`: D column, E line), RespawnShiftX and RespawnShiftY `$FE65` from it, and hides the hero (column 0, line `$8C`, colour 0).

In s2-right 5 deaths, rzx-r2 1.

As in stage 1 at `$B22B`, the same instructions.

Witness: L1 9 (rzx-r2, s2-right).

**E = the neck's segments from its length byte A; a cut neck (bit 7) shrinks one a pass**

A = the length byte (`$FE5C`, `$FE5D` or `$FE5E`: twice the segments). With bit 7 set (the head was killed: `$7FCD`, `$8003`,

#### `DrawNeckHigh` (`$9FC4`)

**Draw E segments of a neck from the pose IX, the lines less n (clipped at the top)**

In: A = the pose, B = the points of a pose, IX = the neck's points, C = the line change (its negative n is written

into the SUB n at NeckLineUp `$9FF3`), E = the segments. IX = IX + pose x 2B (the multiply `$8B4B`). Each segment: a

point (+0 the pixel column from the play area's left, +1 the line); the image is NeckSegments `$C684` + (column AND

7) x 16 (2 bytes x 8 lines, pre-shifted); at line - n it is ORed into the play buffer at `$5B00` + line x 32 +

column / 8 + 6 (OrNeckSegment `$A066`). A segment 1-7 lines above the top is drawn from the line it shows: the CALL

at `$A034` is aimed past the hidden rows (NeckSkipCall), DE past their bytes; one higher is skipped.

Used for the first neck (n = 8) and the second (n = `$38`) in room 7: 764 calls each in rzx-r2. The top clip

(`$9FF8-$A037`) is not executed in any recording (the recordings checked: s2-right, rzx-r2); known only from the code.

#### `FragmentActor` (`$AA81`)

**Per-pass handler of a fragment: fly an arc, land, lie, sink, be picked up**

The handler word of the fragment template (`$975A`). IY = the fragment. Its colour alternates (ColourRedMagenta `$B499`). The step counter +`$0B` runs from 0: steps 5, `$0E`, `$14` and `$17` play effect 3 (a bounce); each step moves it by +8 pixels a pass across (MoveFragment `$AB6A`, reversed when facing left) and down by the step's entry of FragmentArc0 `$ABBA` (arc +`$0A` = 0) or FragmentArc1 `$ABD6` (other arcs; doubled when +`$0A` bit 1 is set); from step `$18` it no longer moves across. At steps 9, `$10`, `$15` and `$17` it looks at the cell under it (column + 2, line + `$16`, `$14` or `$0E`; CellAt `$B2DC`): no solid ground there makes it fall (step `$1C`: 7 lines a pass, removed under line `$90`). Step `$1B` is the rest (FragmentRest `$AB0D`): +`$0E` counts down; under 6 it sinks 3 lines a pass and at 0 it is removed. A fragment the hero touches (his column or the one right of it, his line within `$20`) is taken: EnergyChange `$FE59` + 6, score +25 (`$7B1F`), effect 5, and it is removed.

In rzx-r2 1383 passes (the urns' and the statues' fragments); none in s2-right.

As in stage 1 at `$A891`, the same instructions; the touch looks at the column right of the hero's (INC E at `$AB33`, stage 1 DEC E).

#### `MoveFragment` (`$AB6A`)

**Move the fragment E pixels across and point it at its pre-shifted image**

IY = the fragment, E = the pixels (negated when it faces left, +9 bit 7). The pixel column (+0 x 8 + the sub-column +`$0D`) moves by E; +0 and +`$0D` take the new column and pixel. The image pointer +4/+5 = FragmentSprites `$D264` + `$21` x the shift (the multiply `$8B4B`; the shift is the pixel, or 7 - the pixel when it faces left): eight pre-shifted copies of 33 bytes. A fragment that reaches column 0 or 31 is removed (RemoveActor `$B489`).

#### `UpdatePathFlyer` (`$85A2`)

**Kinds 7 and 8: a flyer along PathSteps, forwards (7) then back (8); OR-drawn 3 x 13 bytes**

+4 = the step into PathSteps (pairs: dx in half columns, dy), +5 = x in half columns, +3 a step counter. Kind 7 steps forwards; at the end mark (`$64`) it becomes kind 8 and is moved by RespawnShiftX (x 2) and RespawnShiftY, unless no lives are left (freed). Kind 8 steps back and is freed at step `$FF`. +0 = +5 / 2; the pre-shifted half (`$B6DD` or `$B6E1` by +5's parity) is ORed into the buffer (3 bytes x 13 lines) when on screen (column under `$1E`, y under `$78`), then coloured (`$B4C5`, `$B748`).

As in stage 1 at `$842C`, the same code.

Witness: L1 5192 (rzx-r2, s2-right).

#### `Unrle` (`$A33D`)

**Unpack an RLE block: the first byte is the escape, ESC n v is n copies of v, ESC ESC ends**

Input: HL = the packed block, DE = the output. The block's first byte is its escape byte, written into UnrleEscape and UnrleEnd's compares. Then: a byte other than the escape is copied; the escape followed by n, v writes n copies of v (n = 0 gives 256); the escape twice ends. Output: HL = the second escape of the end mark, DE = after the output.

RoomChange `$9257` (`$9262`) unpacks the stage's tiles and map StageGraphics `$B7D5` to `$5B00` with it at every room change (7 calls in s2-right, 33 in rzx-r2).

As in stage 1 at `$A424`, the same code.

#### `CopyScreenToBlock` (`$8AAE`)

**Copy a block of the screen, one pixel line at a time, into a buffer**

HL = the buffer (lines packed one after the other), B = the screen column, C = the first pixel line, D = the width

in bytes, E = the lines. Patches its ADD A,n at `$8AC2` with the column; the line addresses come from ScreenLineTable.

Each line: EX DE,HL, LDIR, EX DE,HL, so the screen's bytes go to the buffer. EndStageSave (`$7916`) saves the

HUD's 48 lines into `$7000` with it.

#### `StartBurst` (`$9BFA`)

**Turn a 16 x 12 shape into particles at `$7040` that fly apart (UpdateBurst)**

Input: A = BurstSmall (1 small: 14 steps; 0 big: 28), D, E = the shape's left column and top cell row, IX = the shape (12 rows of 2 bytes, bit 7 left), B and C = the two inks. PlaySoundVector 1, RandomPointer = `$0D7A` (every burst flies the same way), the colours C, C + `$40` (bright), B, B + `$40` into ParticleInks, BurstTimer = `$FF`. Each set bit of the shape gives a particle record of 4 bytes at `$7040`: X, Y (cell row), the direction (a random 0-5, + 13 for the right byte), the ink (a random 0-3); `$FF` ends the list. Preserves IY.

#### `UpdateBurst` (`$9C92`)

**Move and draw the burst's particles one step (every pass)**

Called by the main loop (`$7861`) once a pass. Nothing while BurstTimer `$FE3A` = `$64`. Else BurstTimer + 1; at `$1C` the burst ends (StopBurst `$9D90`). Unlike stage 1 (`$A28B`) the end is `$1C` in both modes: there is no shorter end for the small mode; BurstSmall `$FE3B` only doubles the step index below.

The step picks the particles' glyph: the byte at `$EDC7` + the step + a random 0-3 (Random `$8BAC`) x 8 + `$EDA7`, written into ParticleGlyph (the LD DE,n at `$9D46`). Each particle (4 bytes from `$7040`: +0 the column, +1 the cell row, +2 the direction, +3 the ink 0-3; `$FF` ends the list, `$80` a dead one): its direction's row of 32 at `$EDEA` (directions 0-9 the second set of BurstSteps, `$0A` and up the first, less `$0D`) gives at the step (+ the ink's bits, doubled when BurstSmall) an index into BurstSteps (dx, dy): the column + dx is kept in 1-30, the row - dy dies (`$80`) at 18 and up. The 8 glyph bytes go into the play buffer at the cell (`$5B00` + row x 256 + column, a line every 32 bytes) and ParticleInks[+3] into the cell's attribute (AttrShadowAddressA `$B479`).

In rzx-r2 it draws 453 steps (the bursts of the statues, the urns and the hydra's heads); s2-right has no burst.

As in stage 1 at `$A296` (UpdateBurstStep), the same instructions; stage 1's head with the small-mode end is gone.

Witness: L1 8031 (rzx-r2, s2-right, stageload).

#### `LoadRoomActors` (`$A431`)

**Free the actors not kept over a room change and create the room's placed actors**

Frees every record of `$74F2-$75DB` without +`$0F` bit 1. Then walks Placements (3 bytes: the kind, bit 7 done; X and Y in cells over the whole grid; `$FF` ends). A placement not done inside the room window (X in 2 x RoomColumn to + 29, Y in 2 x RoomRow to + 17) takes a free record found from `$75CA` down (no lower bound: it is assumed there is one) and is filled from ActorKinds `$9607` (9 bytes a kind: Y offset in lines, the handler, five bytes for +8..+`$0C`, +`$0F`): X and Y relative to the room (Y in lines + the offset), the entry X, Y, +`$10` = the placement's index, width 1, height 8, +`$11` = 0, and a random 0-63 (NextSeed `$8B9D`) for +`$0A` when the kind gives `$40` (no stage-2 kind does: not executed in any recording).

Called by RoomChange `$9257` (`$92E8`) at each room change: 7 times in s2-right, 33 in rzx-r2. Stage 2 has 21 kinds (ActorKinds `$9607-$96C3`).

As in stage 1 at `$A4CC`, the same instructions (its own table address).

#### `SetActorFrame` (`$AC52`)

**Set the actor IY to frame A of a frame table (the 4 bytes after the CALL)**

The CALL is followed by two words: the frame table DE and the graphics base BC; the routine pops them and returns to its caller's caller. A frame record is 6 bytes (FrameRecordAddress `$B278`: DE + 6A): +0 the column offset (negated when the actor faces left, +9 bit 7), +1 the line offset, +2 the width in bytes, +3 the height in lines, +4/+5 the offset of the image from the graphics base. The actor's column +0 = the offset + its base column +`$0D`, its line +1 = the line offset + its base line +`$0E`, +2 and +3 the size, +4/+5 the image address. An image is width x height bytes, row by row, one bit a pixel, no mask.

Every actor's frame goes through it: 6475 calls in s2-right, 14847 in rzx-r2.

As in stage 1 at `$AA02`, the same code.

Witness: L1 22570 (rzx-r2, s2-right, stageload).

#### `AddMissile` (`$B3BD`)

**Add a missile (shot, spark) to the first eight slots of the missile records `$75E0`**

In: D column, E line, C type, B and A its parameters. The list holds 16 records of 6 bytes: +0 column (`$FF` free), +1 line, +2 type (the handler of MissileHandlers `$B449`), +3 `$FF`, +4 B, +5 A. The search starts after the slot of MissileCursor `$FE27` (round robin over 8). A = `$FA` puts a Random `$8BAC` byte in +5. Out: Z when the eight slots are full (nothing added), else NZ. AddMissileHigh `$B3C5` uses slots 8-15 (`$7610`).

Called by `$90E0`, AimedShot, FireHeroMissile, HydraHeadShot and KindTwelveShot: 188 in s2-right, 282 in rzx-r2.

### Stage 3 (TZX block 46): entry

`src/stage3/entry.asm`

#### `StageEntry` (`$7800`)

**Start the stage: lives from H, variables, HUD, the first room, the hero placed, then the main loop**

Called by the resident stage loader with H = the lives left. Stores H in Lives, then: InitStageState `$9D00` (the variables, the carried items from StartItems), StageSetUp `$970D` (the title, the HUD), ClearActors `$959F` and ResetObjectLists `$95B0`, RoomGrid = `$9B37` (grid 0, the longship) with Placements = `$9B62` (grid 0's placements), ReviveAllPlacements `$A69F` and PlaceHeroAtStart `$A672`, GridNumber = 0, RoomNumber = 1, StartGrid `$A639` (builds the room), ClearBuffer, RunActorHandlers `$A7BB`, DrawActors `$A7DD` and CopyBuffer, StageFadeIn `$9785`; then the hero record: `$74E3` (+3, the height) = `$16`, the state `$74EA` = 0, the base column `$74ED` = `$0D`; runs on into MainLoop.

Stage 1's StageEntry (`$7800`) has the same job but enters grid 0 at room 2, with no StageFadeIn call and no hero fields of its own (known from the code at `$7826` and `$7839-$7847`).

Witness: L1 2 (rzx-r3, s3-right).

#### `MainLoop` (`$784A`)

**One pass: pace, HUD, input, actors, the stage's hazards, draw, copy; SPACE opens the item window**

The pass, in order: PacePass, ShowPieceTaken, FlashPieces, CheckPause (ENTER), SpawnTimer, RedrawItemsIfChanged, ClearBuffer, CheckStageExit (may leave to EndStage), `$A3FD`, `$A41E`, UpdateMissiles `$B384`, RunActorHandlers `$A7BB`, DrawActors `$A7DD`, DrawDragon (grid 1 room 8), `$9514` (grid 2: the throne giant's picture and its fireballs), UpdateBurst `$A201`, KeyHook, `$A588` (grid 0: the lightning), UpdateAttributes (attributes and CopyBuffer), PassTick `$9815` (energy, lives flash, game over step), ShowScore, then the SPACE test TestSpaceKey.

SPACE with CAPS SHIFT ends the stage with E = 1 (QuitStage); SPACE alone opens ItemWindow while HeroFreeze is 0. The loop goes on while Lives is not 0 or the hero's state `$74EA` is not 0; with no lives and the hero back in state 0 it runs on into GameOverExit (E = 0).

Stage 1's MainLoop at `$7839` has the same frame; it calls DrawArenaPicture, ZoneDamage and DrawRoomPicture where stage 3 calls DrawDragon, `$9514` and `$A588`, and tests the hero's state `$0F` (not HeroFreeze) before the item window.

Witness: L1 6279 (rzx-r3, s3-right).

#### `EndStage` (`$78B6`)

**Leave the stage: hide the HUD boxes, save the HUD, fade, return E, H = lives, BC = the score's digits**

E (pushed) is the outcome: 0 game over (GameOverExit), 1 quit (QuitStage), 2 stage completed (StageExit). Clears the play buffer, hides the pieces boxes and the lives boxes with two inline attribute fills (`$8ADE`), saves the HUD attributes (rows 0-5) to `$7600`, clears the score, the two middle HUD fields, the item strip and the pieces field with CopyToScreen from the cleared buffer (stride 0), saves the HUD bitmap (lines 0-47) to `$7000` (`$892A`), fades the screen (FlashFadeScreen), clears it (`$8A33`), waits 100 frames (`$8AD6`) and returns to the stage loader with E, BC = ScoreDigitsHigh (the six score digits) and H = Lives.

Stage 1's EndStage at `$789E` is the same code.

Witness: L1 2 (rzx-r3, s3-right).

**Reseed the random pointer every 64 passes and pad the pass with a busy wait in grid 1's room 10**

#### `PlotRow1` (`$8633`)

**Plot one sprite row 1 byte wide into the play buffer**

#### `CopyBuffer` (`$9AA2`)

**Copy the open spans of the play buffer to the screen (an LDI chain cut by a patched JP)**

SP walks the span table `$76A0` (POP BC: the length, POP HL: the buffer, POP DE: the screen). For each span: patches

the LD BC at `$9B0D` with 32 - the length, writes JP `$9B0D` into the LDI chain at `$9AD1` + 2 x the length (saved at

`$9B18`), the LD E at `$9B11` with the screen address's low byte; copies 8 lines (LDIs, then HL + 32 - length, E

back, D + 1); puts ED A0 ED back. SpanCount spans; interrupts off meanwhile.

Stage 1's CopyBuffer at `$9ADA`, the same instructions; the operands that differ (`$9AAB`, `$9AB5`, `$9ABA`, `$9ABE`, `$9AC4`, `$9ACC`) are addresses: SpanTable `$76E0` and the routine's own patched instructions (`$9B0E`, `$9AD1`, `$9B18`, `$9B12`), all stage 3's.

#### `DrawActorSprite` (`$A8A8`)

**Draw B lines of the actor's frame into the play buffer, then colour it**

Input: B lines, DE = the buffer, HL = the frame (rows of +2 bytes, top first, no mask). +9 bit 0: copied opaque (DrawActorOpaque). Else ORed in by a row routine from the table `$87CD` (4 bytes a width 0-7: the right-facing and the left-facing routine); the left-facing routines mirror the bytes through the resident bit-reverse table `$FA00` and step left, so a left-facing actor's X is its right column. A shifted copy (+`$11` 1-99) is one byte wider. The routine is written into RowDrawCall. Then ColourActor.

**Copy a block of the screen, one pixel line at a time, into a buffer**

in bytes, E = the lines. Patches its ADD A,n at `$893E` with the column; the line addresses come from ScreenLineTable.

#### `DissolveHud` (`$8952`)

**Dissolve the HUD's 48 pixel lines onto the screen in 8 steps**

DE = the source picture (48 lines of 32 bytes; `$7000` from StageSetUp `$970D`: the HUD as loaded). Eight steps, each

after a HALT: every byte of screen lines 0-47 = source AND a mask; the mask is DissolveMasks `$F9CB` + set + step

(set = bits 3-4 of a ROM byte read through RandomPointer, 0, 8, 16 or 24; the step 0-7, the ADD at DissolveStepOperand set to 0 first) and gains bits each step until `$FF`; only RandomPointer's low byte is cleared each step, so each step reads the next 6 pages of the ROM and the pattern changes (rzx-r1: the first reads of the 8 steps at `$0701`, `$0D01`, `$1301` ... `$3101`). Patches the

LD DE at `$8966` (the source) and the ADD A at `$898A` (the step).

Stage 1's DissolveHud at `$8AB1` is the same code.

Witness: L1 2 (rzx-r3, s3-right).

#### `ItemWindow` (`$7C15`)

**SPACE: stop the game, flash the strip's frame, choose an item with LEFT and RIGHT, SPACE again to go on**

Clears PassCounter, waits (cycling the frame colours, CycleWindowFrame) for SPACE's release, then every 6 frames: DrawItemStrip and ShowItemCount; RIGHT scrolls to the previous slot (ScrollItemsRight), LEFT to the next (ScrollItemsLeft); SPACE again: waits for its release, cycles the frame back to its first colour and flashes the selected box (FlashSelectedBox).

The HUD's strip itself is drawn in every recording (c1 frame 15982).

Stage 1's ItemWindow at `$7C27` is the same code.

#### `ThrowItem` (`$9646`)

**Throw the selected item when the fire key is pressed (one throw a press)**

Called by HeroUpdate (`$AE0E`). FireLatch makes it one throw a press. Unless the hero's state is `$0F`: takes one of the selected

#### `HeroUpdate` (`$ADE3`)

**The hero's pass: items, hazards, weapons, colour, then his state's handler**

IY = the hero. DrainItemCharge `$8860` and the three checks DragonFireDamage `$8807`, CheckWaterDeath `$8824` and PyreFireDamage `$87ED`. #### `ShiftRoomColumns` (`$9E6B`)

#### `Unrle` (`$A39A`)

**Unpack an RLE block: the first byte is the escape, ESC n v is n copies of v, ESC ESC ends**

Input: HL = the packed block, DE = the output. The block's first byte is its escape byte, written into UnrleEscape and UnrleEnd's compares. Then: a byte other than the escape is copied; the escape followed by n, v writes n copies of v (n = 0 gives 256); the escape twice ends. Output: HL = the second escape of the end mark, DE = after the output.

The room builder `$9853` unpacks the stage's tiles and map at `$B556` with it to `$5B00` at every room change (26 calls in the stage-1 recordings).

Stage 1's Unrle at `$A424` is the same code.

Witness: L1 39 (rzx-r3, s3-right).

#### `UpdateRain` (`$A41E`)

**The rain's pass: colour the sky, move and draw the drops, step RainStep; and the rain item of room 5**

Called every main-loop pass (`$7865`) after RainChance. RainStep `$FE5A` 0: UpdateRainIdle. Else: the splash line, `$77`, or `$67` in grid 0's rooms 1 and 2 (the longship's deck), is written into the CP at `$A4A3`; the shadow attributes of the play area's first 15 rows (`$6DC0`, 480 bytes) are set to 5 (cyan ink on black) so the drops are seen; RainStep + 1 (it runs to `$FF` and wraps to 0: the rain ends after 255 passes). In grid 1 or 2, step `$50` sets PyreState `$FE5D` = 1 (the pyre's flames start to die, PyreFlameActor `$93C8`) and step `$64` PyreState 2 (the body may rise, PyreBodyActor `$945E`). The drops drawn: RainStep / 2 + 2 up to step `$7F`, then (`$FF` - RainStep) / 2 + 2, at most `$38`: the rain thickens and thins.

Each drop: line + speed under `$80` and under the splash line: it falls (line + speed, column - speed: slanting left) and is drawn by DrawRainDrop; at the splash line: line = splash line - 3, its splash step +3 + 1 drawn by DrawRainSplash; after step 3 it starts again at a random column, line 0. A line of `$80` and up (above the play area) moves without being drawn.

Witness: L1 6278 (rzx-r3, s3-right).

GetSelectedItem `$7EEA`: kind 9 selected, RoomNumber 5 and a count left: the count - 1 (ShowItemCount `$7D4C`) and StartRain. The fire key is not needed: selecting it in room 5 is enough. rzx-r3 used it once (the fall-through to `$A501` ran 1 time).

#### `FragmentActor` (`$AA94`)

**Per-pass handler of a fragment: fly an arc, land, lie, sink, be picked up**

The handler word of the fragment template `$9CA6` (`$9CAC`). IY = the fragment. Its colour alternates (ColourRedMagenta `$B411`). The step counter +`$0B` runs from 0: steps 5, `$0E`, `$14` and `$17` play effect 3 (a bounce); each step moves it +8 pixels a pass across (MoveFragment `$AB82`, reversed when facing left) and down by the step's entry of FragmentArc0 `$ABD2` (arc +`$0A` = 0) or FragmentArc1 `$ABEE` (other arcs; doubled when +`$0A` bit 1 is set); from step `$18` it no longer moves across. At steps 9, `$10`, `$15` and `$17` it looks at the cell under it (column + 2, line + `$16`, `$14`, `$14` or `$0E`; CellAt `$B1F6`): no solid ground there makes it fall (step `$1C`: 7 lines a pass, removed at line `$90` and below). Step `$1B` is the rest (FragmentRest): +`$0E` counts down; under 6 it sinks 3 lines a pass and at 0 it is removed. A fragment the hero touches (its column the hero's + 1, + 0 or - 1, his line within `$20`) is taken: EnergyChange `$FE51` + 6, AddScore `$7B41` 25, effect 5, and it is removed.

The same job as stage 1's FragmentActor; stage 3's touch test takes three columns (stage 1 two). rzx-r3 broke two urns into fragments (ShatterActor 2 runs) and took 9 fragments.

#### `StartBurst` (`$A169`)

**Turn a 16 x 12 shape into particles at `$7040` that fly apart (UpdateBurst)**

Input: A = BurstSmall (1 small: 14 steps; 0 big: 28), D, E = the shape's left column and top cell row, IX = the shape (12 rows of 2 bytes, bit 7 left), B and C = the two inks. PlaySoundVector 1, RandomPointer = `$0D7A` (every burst flies the same way), the colours C, C + `$40` (bright), B, B + `$40` into ParticleInks, BurstTimer = `$FF`. Each set bit of the shape gives a particle record of 4 bytes at `$7040`: X, Y (cell row), the direction (a random 0-5, + 13 for the right byte), the ink (a random 0-3); `$FF` ends the list. Preserves IY.

#### `UpdateBurst` (`$A201`)

**Move and draw the burst's particles one step (every pass)**

Called by the main loop. Nothing while BurstTimer = `$64`. Else BurstTimer + 1; at the last step (`$1C`, or `$0E` when BurstSmall) it ends (StopBurst). The step picks the particles' glyph: `$EED9`[step + a random 0-3] x 8 + `$EEB9`, written into ParticleGlyph. Each particle (4 bytes from `$7040`, `$FF` ends, `$80` dead): its direction's step table at `$EEFC` + direction x 32 gives an index into BurstSteps (dx, dy; the second set for directions 13 and up), X + dx kept within 1-30, Y - dy (a particle above row 0 or below row 17 dies: `$80`); then the 8 glyph bytes are stored into the play buffer at the cell and the cell's attribute (ParticleInks) via `$B3E8`.

Stage 1's UpdateBurst at `$A28B` is the same code.

#### `LoadRoomActors` (`$A6CA`)

**Free the actors not kept over a room change and create the room's placed actors**

Frees every record of `$74F2-$75DB` without +`$0F` bit 1. Then walks Placements (3 bytes: the kind, bit 7 done; X and Y in cells over the whole grid; `$FF` ends). #### `SetActorFrame` (`$AC0A`)

**Set the actor IY to frame A of a frame table (the 4 bytes after the CALL)**

The CALL is followed by two words: the frame table DE and the graphics base BC; the routine pops them and

returns to its caller's caller. A frame record is 6 bytes (FrameRecordAddress `$B1BE`: DE + 6A): +0 the column

offset (negated when the actor faces left, +9 bit 7), +1 the line offset, +2 the width in bytes, +3 the height in

lines, +4/+5 the offset of the image from the graphics base. The actor's column +0 = the offset + its base column

+`$0D`, its line +1 = the line offset + its base line +`$0E`, +2 and +3 the size, +4/+5 the image address. An image is

width x height bytes, row by row, one bit a pixel, no mask (DrawSprite `$B4EA` copies it).

Stage 1's SetActorFrame at `$AA02` is the same code.

**Start the stage: lives from H, variables, HUD, the first room, then the main loop**

Called by the resident stage loader with H = the lives left. RoomNumber stays 0 (cleared by InitStageState).

### Stage 4 (TZX block 49): mainloop

`src/stage4/mainloop.asm`

#### `MainLoop` (`$7837`)

**One pass: pace, HUD, input, actors, draw, copy; SPACE opens the item window**

The pass, in order: PacePass, ShowPieceTaken, FlashPieces, CheckPause (ENTER), SpawnTimer `$9245`, RedrawItemsIfChanged, ClearBuffer `$9A28`, CheckStageExit (may leave to StageExit), UpdateMissiles `$B4AC`, TrapChainStep, RunActorHandlers `$A746`, LinkTrapSlots, DrawBossPicture, DrawActors `$A768`, `$B412`, `$A41D`, KeyHook, UpdateAttributes (attributes and CopyBuffer), PassTick `$97BD` (energy, lives flash, game over step), ShowScore, then the SPACE test TestSpaceKey.

SPACE with CAPS SHIFT (port `$FEFE` bit 0) ends the stage with E = 1 (QuitStage); SPACE alone opens ItemWindow (stage 1 also refused it while the hero was dying; stage 4 does not test the hero's state). The loop goes on while Lives is not 0 or the hero's state `$74EA` is not 0; with no lives and the hero back in state 0 it falls into GameOverExit. s4-right ran 945 passes and ended at the game over (217 passes with no lives left before the hero's state came back to 0); rzx-r4 ran 7675 passes, opened the item window 20 times and left through CheckStageExit.

Witness: L1 8620 (rzx-r4, s4-right).

#### `EndStage` (`$7898`)

**Leave the stage: hide the pieces boxes, then EndStageSave (save the HUD, fade) returns E, H = lives, BC = the score's digits**

E (pushed) is the outcome: 0 game over (GameOverExit), 1 quit (QuitStage), 2 stage completed (StageExit `$7A72`). ClearBuffer `$9A28`, then the pieces boxes' attributes (rows 3 and 4, columns 25-30: `$5879` and `$5899`, 6 cells each) set to 1 with two LDIRs. Stage 1 hid the lives boxes too with two inline FillAttributes records; stage 4 hides only the pieces boxes and falls straight into EndStageSave.

#### `EndStageSave` (`$78B6`)

**EndStage, continued: save the HUD, clear its fields, fade, return**

Saves the HUD's attributes (rows 0-5, 192 bytes) to `$7600`. Clears five HUD fields with CopyToScreen from the cleared play buffer `$5B00` (stride 0): the score (column 6, line 8, 6 x 8), the fields at column `$0E` (4 x 8) and column `$14` (6 x 8) of line 8, the item strip (column `$0A`, line `$18`, 12 x 16) and the pieces field (column `$19`, line `$18`, 6 x 16). Then CopyScreenToBlock saves lines 0-47 into the HUD picture (`$7000`, 32 x 48), FlashFadeScreen, ClearScreen, WaitFrames 100. Returns with E = the outcome (popped), BC = ScoreDigitsHigh (the score's six digits as text) and H = Lives.

#### `PacePass` (`$7961`)

**Pad the pass with a busy wait taken from PaceWaits by grid and room**

BC = PaceWaits[GridNumber x 3 + RoomNumber], then BC is counted down to 0 (PacePassWait, 24 T-states a round: JP NZ is 10 T). Grid 0 room 0 waits `$0258` rounds, grid 0 room 1 `$0640`, grid 4 rooms 0 and 1 `$04B0`, every other place 1. Unlike stage 1's PacePass (which also reseeded RandomPointer from R every 64 passes and used DelayBC), stage 4's has its own loop and no reseed. The busy wait ran 1 498 000 rounds in s4-right's 945 passes (grid 0) and 1 099 377 in rzx-r4's 7675.

Witness: L1 8620 (rzx-r4, s4-right).

#### `CheckPause` (`$79E2`)

**ENTER pauses: wait for its release, a second press and its release**

Reads port `$BFFE` bit 0 (ENTER). Not pressed: returns at once. Pressed: waits for the key's release, the next press and its release, so the game stands still between two presses. No other effect. As in stage 1 at `$79B1`. The wait loops from `$79EA` on ran in neither recording (ENTER never pressed).

#### `FlashFadeScreen` (`$7929`)

**Fade every coloured ink up to white over 7 frames, then down to black over 7 frames**

Seven times (HALT each): every attribute whose ink is neither 0 nor 7 gets ink + 1. Then seven times (two HALTs each): every ink not 0 gets ink - 1. Inputs: none; changes the whole attribute area `$5800-$5AFF`. Called by EndStageSave `$7914`. As in stage 1 at `$7925`.

#### `CopyToScreen` (`$79FD`)

**Copy a block of bytes to the screen, line by line**

Inputs: HL = the source, B = the screen column, C = the first pixel line, D = the width in bytes, E = the lines, A = the source's stride (added to HL after each line; 0 repeats one source line, used with the cleared buffer to clear a screen block). Patches the column into the ADD A,n at `$7A15` and the stride into the LD C,n at `$7A26`, then for each line takes the line's address from ScreenLineTable and LDIRs D bytes. Destroys IX, A, BC, DE. Callers: EndStageSave, ShowScore, ShowItemCount, ShowPieceTaken, GameOverStep and the score reveal `$97E1`, `$97F1`.

#### `PreShiftSprite` (`$7F89`)

**For an actor with a shift (+`$11` = 1-7): copy its sprite to `$7640` and shift it right**

IY = the actor record. +`$11` = 0 or `$64` and up: nothing. Else copies the sprite (+4/+5, +2 bytes wide, +3 lines) to `$7640` with a zero byte added to each line, then shifts each line right by +`$11` pixels with the routine ShiftRoutines[+`$11`] (patched into PreShiftCall). Called by `$A7D0` for every actor drawn. As in stage 1 at `$7F4D`.

Witness: L1 67987 (rzx-r4, s4-right).

#### `PlotRow1` (`$8D71`)

**Plot one sprite row 1 byte wide into the play buffer**

HL = the sprite's bytes, DE = the buffer address. ORs (HL) into (DE) (no mask: the buffer is cleared every pass), then HL + 1 and DE + 32 (the next pixel line). One of the row plotters of RowPlotters `$8F0B`, read by the sprite drawer at `$A850`. The plotters 1-7 bytes wide all work so; the mirrored ones write the row right to left through the bit-reversal table at `$FA00` (resident), so a sprite faces left. As in stage 1 at `$8776`.

#### `CopyBuffer` (`$9A4D`)

**Copy the open spans of the play buffer to the screen (an LDI chain cut by a patched JP)**

SP walks the span table `$76A0` (POP BC: the length, POP HL: the buffer, POP DE: the screen). For each span: patches CopyLineEnd's LD BC with 32 - the length, writes JP CopyLineEnd into CopyChain at 2 x the length (its address kept in CopySpanRestore's LD HL), and CopyLineE's LD E with the screen address's low byte; copies 8 lines (LDIs, then HL + 32 - length, E back, D + 1); puts ED A0 ED back. SpanCount spans; interrupts off meanwhile. As in stage 1 at `$9ADA`.

#### `CheckStageExit` (`$7A2D`)

**With item 5 selected, in grid 8 room 1 at columns `$10-$13`: leave the stage**

Every pass. Only with item 5 selected (GetSelectedItem), in grid 8 (GridNumber) room 1 and with the hero's x (`$74E0`) from `$10` to `$13`: drops its own return address and runs StageExit (falls into it). Stage 1 tested item 6 at the stage's first room and the hero's y too. Item 5 is the item RoomEvents `$8212` gives in grid 9 once the five pieces are taken (SpawnItem with kind 5). In rzx-r4 the whole test passed once, at the end of the run (pass 7675), and the stage was left through StageExit; s4-right never had item 5 selected.

StartStageExit draws the field and seeds 80 stars at `$5B00` (4 bytes each); then each frame (HALT) moves the stars of speed 1-3 (MoveStar; a speed-4 star stays), until KeyFire or TestSpaceKey reports a key; then E = 2 and EndStage. As in stage 1 at `$7A1D`, with stage 4's addresses.

Witness: L1 1 (rzx-r4).

#### `MoveStar` (`$7A75`)

**Move one star down by its speed and plot it as two pixel lines**

IX = the star: +0 speed 1-4, +1 the pixel within the byte 0-3, +2 the column 2-29, +3 y (`$80` and up: not yet on screen). Off screen: y += speed only. On screen: y = (y + speed) mod 128; IY = ScreenLineTable + 96 + 2y (line 48 + y); clears the star's column on speed lines from there down, then plots the two lines StarPixels[(speed - 1) x 8 + pixel x 2] under them. As stage 1's MoveStar `$7A4A`.

Witness: L1 5974 (rzx-r4).

#### `DissolveHud` (`$8FD6`)

**Dissolve the HUD's 48 pixel lines onto the screen in 8 steps**

DE = the source picture (48 lines of 32 bytes; `$7000` from StageSetUp `$9732`: the HUD as loaded). Eight steps, each after a HALT: every byte of screen lines 0-47 = source AND a mask; the mask is DissolveMasks `$F9CB` + set + step (set = bits 3-4 of a ROM byte read through RandomPointer, 0, 8, 16 or 24; the step 0-7, the ADD at DissolveStepOperand set to 0 first) and gains bits each step until `$FF`; only RandomPointer's low byte is cleared each step, so each step reads the next 6 pages of the ROM and the pattern changes (rzx-r1: the first reads of the 8 steps at `$0701`, `$0D01`, `$1301` ... `$3101`). Patches the LD DE at `$8FEC` (the source) and the ADD A at DissolveStepOperand (the step). As stage 1's DissolveHud `$8AB1`.

Witness: L1 2 (rzx-r4, s4-right).

#### `Unrle` (`$A5AC`)

**Unpack an RLE block: the first byte is the escape, ESC n v is n copies of v, ESC ESC ends**

Input: HL = the packed block, DE = the output. The block's first byte is its escape byte, written into UnrleEscape and UnrleEnd's compares. A byte other than the escape is copied; the escape followed by n, v writes n copies of v (n = 0 gives 256); the escape twice ends. RoomChange `$9806` unpacks the stage's tiles and map at `$B77F` to `$5B00` with it at every room change. As in stage 1 at `$A424`.

(In grid 3 the other rooms reach `$A96A` with RoomNumber in A, so room 4 leaves kind 8 there too.) Then frame +8 of StrikeableActorSet. As in stage 1 at `$A7C4`, which leaves other items.

#### `FragmentActor` (`$AA4C`)

**Per-pass handler of a fragment: fly an arc, land, lie, sink, be picked up**

The handler word of the template `$9F17`. Its colour alternates (ColourRedMagenta `$B530`). The step +`$0B` runs from 0: steps 5, `$0E`, `$14` and `$17` play effect 3 (a bounce); each step moves it +8 pixels across (MoveFragment) and down by the step's entry of FragmentArc0 (arc 0) or FragmentArc1 (other arcs; doubled when +`$0A` bit 1 is set); from step `$18` it no longer moves across. At steps 9, `$10`, `$15` and `$17` it looks at the cell under it (CellAt `$B346`): no solid ground makes it fall (step `$1C`: 7 lines a pass, removed at line `$90`). Step `$1B` is the rest: +`$0E` counts down; under 6 it sinks 3 lines a pass and at 0 it is removed. One the hero touches (his column or the one left of it, his line within `$20`) is taken: EnergyChange + 6, AddScore `$7B94` with 25, effect 5, removed. As in stage 1 at `$A891`.

Not executed in any recording (the recordings checked: s4-right, rzx-r4); known only from the code.

#### `MoveFragment` (`$AB35`)

**Move the fragment E pixels across and point it at its pre-shifted image**

IY = the fragment, E = the pixels (negated when it faces left). The pixel column (+0 x 8 + +`$0D`) moves by E; +0 and +`$0D` take the new column and pixel. The image +4/+5 = `$E177` + `$21` x the shift (Multiply `$904B`; the shift is the pixel, or 7 - the pixel facing left): eight pre-shifted copies of 33 bytes. A fragment at column 0 or 31 and up is removed (RemoveActor `$B520`). As in stage 1 at `$A97A`.

#### `SetActorFrame` (`$ABBD`)

**Set the actor IY to frame A of a frame table (the 4 bytes after the CALL)**

The CALL is followed by two words: the frame table DE and the graphics base BC; the routine pops them and returns to its caller's caller. A frame record is 6 bytes (FrameRecordAddress `$B2E2`: DE + 6A): +0 the column offset (negated when the actor faces left, +9 bit 7), +1 the line offset, +2 the width in bytes, +3 the height in lines, +4/+5 the offset of the image from the base. The actor's +0 = the offset + its base column +`$0D`, +1 = the line offset + its base line +`$0E`, +2 and +3 the size, +4/+5 the image address. As in stage 1 at `$AA02`.

Witness: L1 62837 (rzx-r4, s4-right).

#### `StartBurst` (`$A385`)

**Turn a 16 x 12 shape into particles at `$7040` that fly apart (UpdateBurst)**

Input: A = BurstSmall (1 small, 0 big), D, E = the shape's left column and top cell row, IX = the shape (12 rows of 2 bytes, bit 7 left), B and C = the two inks. PlaySoundVector 1, RandomPointer = `$0D7A` (every burst flies the same way), the colours C, C + `$40`, B, B + `$40` into ParticleInks, BurstTimer = `$FF`. Each set bit of the shape gives a particle record of 4 bytes at `$7040`: the column, the cell row, the direction (a random 0-5, + 13 for the right byte), the ink (a random 0-3); `$FF` ends the list. Frees the actor IY (+0 = `$FF`); preserves IY. As in stage 1 at `$A1F3`.

#### `UpdateBurst` (`$A41D`)

**Move and draw the burst's particles one step (every pass)**

Called by the main loop `$7864`. Nothing while BurstTimer = `$64`. Else BurstTimer + 1; at `$1C` it ends (StopBurst; stage 4 has no shorter end for the small mode). The step picks the particles' glyph: `$E85A`[step + a random 0-3] x 8 + `$E83A`, written into ParticleGlyph. Each particle (4 bytes from `$7040`, `$FF` ends, `$80` dead): its direction's step list at `$E87D` + direction x 32 (index the step + its ink bits, doubled when BurstSmall) gives an index into BurstSteps (dx, dy; the second ten for directions 13 and up); the column + dx is kept within 1-30, the row - dy (outside rows 0-17 the particle dies: `$80`); then the 8 glyph bytes go into the play buffer and the cell's attribute (ParticleInks[ink]) into the shadow (AttrShadowAddressA `$B510`). As in stage 1 at `$A28B`.

#### `LoadRoomActors` (`$A654`)

**Free the actors not kept over a room change and create the room's placed actors**

Jumped to from RoomChange `$988C`. Frees every record of `$74F2-$75DB` without +`$0F` bit 1. #### `AddMissile` (`$B454`)

**Add a missile (shot, spark) to the first eight slots of the missile records `$75E0`**

In: D column, E line, C type, B and A its parameters. 16 records of 6 bytes: +0 column (`$FF` free), +1 line, +2 type (MissileHandlers), +3 `$FF`, +4 B, +5 A. ## Stage 5 (TZX block 52) (`src/stage5/stage5.json`)

resident stage loader over `$6C3F-$F03E` (tools/image.py). Its entries are `src/stage5/<module>.asm`, written from

run's stage 5 replayed pass by pass, the duel won), `work/stage2/rec/ending` (ending: stage 5 from snap5 with POKEs
of the hit counter, the ending texts).

### Stage 5 (TZX block 52): entry

`src/stage5/entry.asm`

#### `StageEntry` (`$7800`)

**Start the stage: lives from H, variables, HUD, duel, texts, hero, stars, then the main loop**

Called by the resident stage loader with H = the lives left. Stores H in Lives (`$FE58`), then: InitStageState `$96DD` (clears `$FE08-$FE56`, the carried items from StartItems, the energy refill `$2E` in EnergyChange `$FE53`), StageSetUp `$95E4` (the title, the HUD, the item strip rolled in, the score revealed), QuietPasses `$965D` (30 idle passes of 3 frames: the HUD's energy refill and lives flash run). Then FireLatch `$FE3A` = 0, Dameron's X DameronX `$FE3E` = 0 and Y DameronY `$FE3F` = `$8E` (below the play area), the path index DameronPathIndex `$FE40` = `$FF`, the phase DuelPhase `$FE43` = `$FF` (the intro text), the text timer DuelTimer `$FE45` = `$044C`, the burst timer BurstTimer `$FE49` = `$65` (idle).

Then DrawIntroText `$8DAF` and DrawEndingText `$8DDE` (the intro and the ending texts drawn into the play buffer at PlayBuffer `$5B00` and `$6200`), ClearHeroShots, InitHero, ClearMissiles, InitStars, and falls into MainLoop.

Witness: L1 3 (ending, rzx-r5, s5-right).

### Stage 5 (TZX block 52): mainloop

`src/stage5/mainloop.asm`

#### `MainLoop` (`$7843`)

**One pass: HALT, the hero, the shots, the stars, Dameron, the HUD, the missiles, the colours; CAPS SHIFT + SPACE quits**

The pass, in order: PassCounter `$FE4D` + 1, HALT, HeroControl, HeroFire, MoveShots, DrawShots, MoveStars, DameronFire, ApplyEnergyChange, DrawEnergyBar `$9744` (the energy bar), LivesFlashStep, DrawStars, DuelStep (the texts or Dameron), UpdateBurst `$9076` (the burst particles); then writes `$02` and `$FF` to the screen bytes `$4200-$4201` (pixel line 2, columns 0-1, in the HUD); TextPassDelay when the phase DuelPhase `$FE43` is `$FF` (the intro) and again when it is 4 (won); DrawHero, UpdateDameronMissiles, ColourPlayArea (which ends in DuelHit).

Then: the hero's game-over count HeroGameOverCount `$BA84` at 0 ends the stage with E = 0 (GameOverExit). CAPS SHIFT (port `$FEFE` bit 0) and SPACE (port `$7FFE` bit 0) both held end it with E = 1 (QuitStage). SPACE alone does nothing: stage 5 has no item window (ItemWindow has no caller).

Witness: L1 11697 (ending, rzx-r5, s5-right).

#### `EndStage` (`$78B5`)

**Leave the stage: hide the HUD boxes, save the HUD, fade, return E, H = lives, BC = the score's digits**

As in stage 1 at `$789E`, the same code with stage 5's addresses. E (pushed) is the outcome: 0 game over (GameOverExit), 1 quit (QuitStage). Clears the play buffer (ClearBuffer `$96AC`), hides the pieces boxes and the lives boxes with two inline attribute fills (FillAttributes `$954E`, EndPiecesBox and EndLivesBox), copies the HUD attributes (rows 0-5, `$5800-$58BF`) to HudColours `$7600`, clears the score (column 6, line 8, 6 x 8 bytes), the two middle HUD fields (column 14, 4 x 8; column 20, 6 x 8), the item strip (column 10, line 24, 12 x 16) and the pieces field (column 25, line 24, 6 x 16) with CopyToScreen from the cleared buffer PlayBuffer `$5B00` (stride 0).

Then saves the HUD bitmap (lines 0-47, 32 bytes wide) to HudPicture `$7000` with CopyScreenToBlock `$93F3` (over the missile records, no longer needed), fades the screen (FlashFadeScreen), clears it (ClearScreen `$949F`), waits 100 frames (WaitFrames `$9546`) and returns to the stage loader with E, BC = ScoreDigitsHigh (the six score digits) and H = Lives.

Not executed in any recording (the recordings checked: s5-right, rzx-r5, ending); known only from the code.

#### `PaceLateForms` (`$7ABB`)

**Pad the pass in Dameron's form 3 and after: wait `$0320` rounds (phase 3) or `$07D0` (phase 4)**

Reached by a JP from DuelStep (`$8855`) with A = the phase DuelPhase `$FE43`, 3 or more: form 3 (no face drawn) and the end cost less, so the pass is padded with a busy count of HL down to 0 (24 T-states a round: DEC HL, LD A,L, OR H, JP NZ): `$07D0` when A is 4, else `$0320`. Returns to DuelStep's caller.

Witness: L1 472 (ending, rzx-r5).

#### `FlashFadeScreen` (`$793C`)

**Fade every coloured ink up to white over 7 frames, then down to black over 7 frames**

As in stage 1 at `$7925`, the same code. Seven times (HALT each): every attribute whose ink is neither 0 nor 7 gets ink + 1. Then seven times (two HALTs each): every ink not 0 gets ink - 1. Inputs: none; changes the attributes `$5800-$5AFF`. Called by EndStage.

#### `CopyToScreen` (`$7979`)

**Copy a block of bytes to the screen, line by line**

As in stage 1 at `$79CC`, the same code. Inputs: HL = the source, B = the screen column, C = the first pixel line, D = the width in bytes, E = the lines, A = the source's stride (added to HL after each line; 0 repeats one source line, used with the cleared buffer to clear a screen block). Patches the column into `$7992` and the stride into `$79A3`, then for each line takes the line's address from ScreenLineTable and LDIRs D bytes. Destroys IX, BC, DE.

Callers: EndStage, ShowScore, ShowItemCount, GameOverStep and RevealScore `$967E` (the score revealed at the start).

Witness: L1 48 (ending, rzx-r5, s5-right).

#### `DuelHit` (`$79A9`)

**Take one pending hit a pass: count it, step the form every 20, flash Dameron's cells blue; while a text is up flash it instead**

Reached by a JP from ColourPlayArea every pass. TextShown `$FE47` = 1 (a text page on screen, set by ShowTexts `$8C87`): FlashTextRows and return. Else when the pending hits PendingHits `$FE41` are 0: return. Else PendingHits `$FE41` - 1 and the hit counter HitCounter `$FE44` + 1; at `$14` (20): HitCounter `$FE44` = 0, the phase DuelPhase `$FE43` + 1, FormChanged `$FE42` = 1 and NextDameronForm `$A0C4` (effect 0 and the bursts of the beaten form; the final burst at phase 4).

Then (DuelHitFlash) the 15 x 16 cells from `$58C0` + (Y AND `$F8`) x 4 + (X + `$78`) / 8 (Dameron's face and dome) get attribute 1 (blue on black) for this pass; ColourPlayArea recolours them on the next.

A shot gives two hits (MoveShots sets PendingHits `$FE41` to 2), so a form takes 10 shots and the duel 40. s5-right never hit Dameron (`$79B7` never ran); rzx-r5 counted all 80 hits (`$79B7` 80 runs, 40 shots on the hit line) and won the duel.

Witness: L1 11696 (ending, rzx-r5, s5-right).

#### `DuelStep` (`$87C2`)

**The texts' timer, or Dameron: his approach and path, his three parts, the late forms' pacing**

Phase `$FF` (the intro), or 4 (won) with FormChanged `$FE42` at 0: the text timer (DuelTextTimer): the timer DuelTimer `$FE45` - 2 a pass and JP ShowTexts `$8C87` (the text pages), until it is `$00A0`. Then won stays on the ending (ShowTexts `$8C87` every pass, the timer no longer counts); the intro starts the duel: the phase = 0, the timer = `$FFC3` (so after the duel the ending waits while the timer's high byte is `$FF` or `$FE` before ShowTexts `$8C87` shows it).

Else (DuelMove): until the arrival flag DameronArrived `$FE3D` is set, Y - 1 a pass (DameronApproachStep) to `$14`, where DameronArrived `$FE3D` = 1; then the path index DameronPathIndex `$FE40` + 1 and X, Y += DameronPath[DameronPathIndex `$FE40`]. HL = ScreenLinePlay `$9805` + 2 x Y (Dameron's top line, from line 48), DrawDameronFace, DrawDameronBack, DrawDameronDome; in form 3 and on PaceLateForms.

s5-right: 470 intro passes, the approach from `$8E` to `$14` in 122 passes, then the path.
